as_told.title: Gimbal eyewitness accounts match the reconstructed trajectory

plain: In 2015, off the coast of Florida, Navy jet crews filmed an object in what became known as the Gimbal video, named for the way the object seems to rotate on screen. The story here is an argument about its flight path. A researcher named Merrick von Rennenkampf, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in a debate with a skeptic, says the path in the video is a vertical U-turn, which he calls a J-hook. He says this matches exactly what the aircrew said the object tracked on radar did. He makes the point twice in the same debate. The second time, he describes it as a striking match with what the eyewitnesses said: the object reversed direction without making any turning curve at all. If his reading is right, the video would back up the crews' accounts of something moving in a way normal aircraft cannot.
